lead: Deleting a rule strands `rule:` citations in files nothing may rewrite — a frozen record's body, a retired goal's `.md` — and `records.py --check` also refuses the dead id in the creating record's `changes.creates`.
body: `rules.py --check` scans `docs/**/*.md` whole, so "frozen history is never edited" and "no citation dangles" cannot both hold. Drop the `rule:` prefix in the frozen prose — the id still reads as a name — and delete it from `changes.creates`, which is the machine-read relation, not the reasoning.
